## User Scenarios & Testing

### User Story 1 - Uncle Mat Creates Story with AI (Priority: P1)

An adult (Uncle Mat) creates a new story using an AI-powered chat interface. The Uncle Mat converses with the AI to produce a complete narrative story (fairy tale, moral story, or short story) with structured elements including characters, setting, plot structure, moral/lesson, and style. The system outputs both the complete story text and structured metadata defining all story elements. The Uncle Mat can review and edit any story elements before finalizing.

**Why this priority**: This is the foundation of the entire experience. Without stories, there is no content for Libbers to interact with. This user journey delivers immediate value as it allows adults to create content.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by creating a chat session, generating a complete story with metadata, editing story elements, and saving the final story. Delivers value as a standalone story creation tool.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** an Uncle Mat has logged in, **When** they start a new story creation session, **Then** the AI chat interface opens and provides prompts to help define story type, theme, and key elements
2. **Given** the Uncle Mat is in a chat session, **When** they describe their desired story concept, **Then** the AI generates a complete story with beginning/middle/end, defined characters (main characters and antagonist/obstacle), setting, style, and moral/lesson
3. **Given** the AI has generated a story, **When** the Uncle Mat reviews the output, **Then** they see both the complete story text and a structured form showing all story elements (characters, setting, plot points, moral, style)
4. **Given** the Uncle Mat is viewing story elements, **When** they edit any element (e.g., change a character name, modify the moral, adjust the setting), **Then** the changes are reflected in both the structured data and story text
5. **Given** the Uncle Mat has reviewed and edited the story, **When** they save the story, **Then** the story is persisted and ready for the madlibization workflow

---

### User Story 2 - Uncle Mat Madlibizes Story (Priority: P2)

After creating a story, the Uncle Mat uses an AI-assisted workflow to identify and create blanks in the story. The system suggests words that could become blanks (adjectives, nouns, verbs, and other parts of speech), and the Uncle Mat selects which suggestions to use or manually adds blanks. The system follows best practices for creating engaging mad lib blanks. Once blanks are finalized, the Uncle Mat submits the story to make it available to Libbers.

**Why this priority**: This transforms static stories into interactive learning experiences. Without this step, stories cannot be shared with Libbers. It builds on P1 and creates the interactive content foundation.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by taking an existing story, running the madlibization workflow, approving/editing suggested blanks, and submitting the story. Delivers value as a mad lib creator tool that works with any existing story.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** an Uncle Mat has a finalized story, **When** they initiate the madlibization workflow, **Then** the AI analyzes the story and suggests specific words to convert into blanks with their part of speech labeled
2. **Given** the system has suggested blanks, **When** the Uncle Mat reviews suggestions, **Then** they see each suggestion highlighted in context with the part of speech and a brief explanation of why it makes a good blank
3. **Given** the Uncle Mat is reviewing blank suggestions, **When** they approve, reject, or manually add blanks, **Then** the story updates to show which words will be blanks and what part of speech each requires
4. **Given** blanks have been defined, **When** the Uncle Mat submits the story, **Then** the story is marked as ready for Libbers and Libbers receive notifications

---

### User Story 3 - Libber Completes Learning Session and Fills Blanks (Priority: P3)

A child (Libber) receives a notification that they have blanks to fill out. The app presents blanks in sessions of three words. For each blank, the Libber completes an educational activity that teaches them about that part of speech, potentially including mini-games and examples. After completing the learning activity, the Libber provides their word for that blank using voice input (with text fallback). The session ends with positive feedback and a notification promise about upcoming results.

**Why this priority**: This is the core learning experience for children. It builds on P1 and P2 by consuming the created content. While critical for the full experience, it depends on stories being created and madlibized first.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by presenting a mock set of three blanks, completing learning activities, submitting words via voice/text, and receiving session completion feedback. Delivers value as an educational parts-of-speech learning tool.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a Libber has blanks to fill out, **When** they open the app or tap the notification, **Then** they enter a session showing three blanks to complete
2. **Given** the Libber is in a session, **When** they start working on a blank, **Then** the app provides audio narration explaining the part of speech and shows an educational activity
3. **Given** the Libber is learning about a part of speech, **When** they engage with mini-games or examples, **Then** their progress and performance are tracked and saved for the Uncle Mat to review
4. **Given** the Libber has completed the learning activity, **When** they provide their word via voice or text, **Then** the word is accepted and saved for that blank
5. **Given** the Libber has completed all three blanks in the session, **When** the session ends, **Then** they receive positive feedback and are told they'll receive a notification when they can see the results

---

### User Story 4 - Libber Views AI-Generated Video of Their Contribution (Priority: P4)

After a Libber completes a session, the system generates an AI-created cartoon video for each Libber showing that portion of the story with their specific word choices. When the video is ready, the Libber receives a notification and can view their personalized video segment.

**Why this priority**: This provides immediate gratification and engagement for children, showing them the impact of their word choices. It's a key motivational feature but can be implemented after the core educational loop is working.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by submitting mock Libber words, waiting for video generation, receiving notification, and viewing the generated video. Delivers value as a personalized content creation experience.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a Libber has completed a session with three words, **When** the video generation process completes, **Then** the Libber receives a notification that their video is ready
2. **Given** the Libber has a ready video, **When** they open the notification or navigate to their videos, **Then** they can view an AI-generated cartoon showing that story segment with their words incorporated
3. **Given** multiple Libbers have submitted words for the same blanks, **When** videos are generated, **Then** each Libber has their own unique video reflecting their personal word choices

---

### User Story 5 - Uncle Mat Selects Final Words and Provides Feedback (Priority: P5)

The Uncle Mat reviews all Libber submissions for each blank, viewing each Libber's video. They decide which word(s) become the final version of the story, with the option to combine words from different Libbers if possible. The Uncle Mat sends personalized messages to each Libber providing encouragement and constructive feedback about their word choices.

**Why this priority**: This creates the social connection and educational feedback loop. While important for the full experience, it depends on all previous steps being complete.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by presenting mock Libber submissions with videos, selecting final words, combining if applicable, and sending feedback messages. Delivers value as a review and curation tool.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** all Libbers have submitted words for a blank, **When** the Uncle Mat views the submissions, **Then** they see each Libber's word choice and can play their associated video
2. **Given** the Uncle Mat is reviewing submissions, **When** they select a final word for a blank, **Then** the story is updated with that word as the canonical choice
3. **Given** the Uncle Mat sees potential for combining words, **When** they choose to combine submissions, **Then** the system generates a new combined video reflecting both word choices
4. **Given** the Uncle Mat has reviewed a Libber's submission, **When** they write a feedback message, **Then** the message is sent to that specific Libber with encouragement and suggestions

---

### User Story 6 - Uncle Mat Assembles Final Story Book (Priority: P6)

Once all blanks are filled and final words selected, the Uncle Mat assembles the complete story into a digital "book" format. They arrange the selected video clips in sequence, add AI-generated still images as transitions or supplementary illustrations, and record audio narration (either their own voice or text-to-speech) that plays over the entire story.

**Why this priority**: This is the culmination of the entire creative journey. It depends on all previous steps and represents the final deliverable. While important, it's the last step in the workflow.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by taking a complete story with selected words and videos, arranging clips, adding transition images, recording/generating voiceover, and producing the final story book. Delivers value as a digital book creation tool.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** all blanks have final words selected, **When** the Uncle Mat enters the story assembly interface, **Then** they see all video clips in story order with options to add transitions
2. **Given** the Uncle Mat is assembling the story, **When** they add AI-generated still images between clips, **Then** the images are inserted as transitions or "glue" moments
3. **Given** the story structure is complete, **When** the Uncle Mat records audio narration or generates TTS, **Then** the audio is synchronized with the visual timeline
4. **Given** the Uncle Mat has finished assembly, **When** they finalize the story book, **Then** a complete digital story book is created combining videos, images, and narration

---

### User Story 7 - Libbers View Final Story Book Together (Priority: P7)

Once the Uncle Mat has finished the story book, all Libbers are notified and can view the complete finished product. They can see how their individual word choices contributed to the larger narrative and enjoy the full story experience.

**Why this priority**: This provides closure to the experience and demonstrates the collaborative nature. It's the final reward but depends entirely on all other steps being complete.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by sharing a completed story book with mock Libbers and allowing them to view it. Delivers value as a content sharing and viewing experience.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the Uncle Mat has finalized a story book, **When** the story is published, **Then** all Libbers in the group receive a notification
2. **Given** a Libber has received a story completion notification, **When** they open the story book, **Then** they can view the complete story with all videos, images, and narration
3. **Given** a Libber is viewing the story book, **When** they see their contributed words, **Then** those moments are highlighted or marked to show their personal contribution

---

### Edge Cases

- What happens when a Libber submits an inappropriate word for a blank?
- How does the system handle a Libber starting but not completing a session?
- What if an Uncle Mat wants to restart the madlibization process after blanks have already been submitted?
- How are notifications handled if a Libber has notifications disabled or is offline for extended periods?
- What happens when video generation fails or takes longer than expected?
- How does the system handle multiple Uncle Mats collaborating on a single story?
- What if a Libber needs to change their submitted word before the Uncle Mat has reviewed it?
- How are incomplete stories handled if an Uncle Mat abandons the creation process partway through?
- What happens when the AI chat generates inappropriate content during story creation?
- How does the app handle poor or no internet connectivity during voice input?
- What if multiple Libbers submit words simultaneously for the same blank?
- How does the system handle age-appropriate content filtering for different age groups of Libbers?

## Requirements

### Functional Requirements

#### User Management & Groups

- **FR-001**: System MUST support two distinct user roles: Uncle Mats (adults) and Libbers (children)
- **FR-002**: System MUST allow users to create and join groups with one or more Uncle Mats and one or more Libbers
- **FR-003**: System MUST allow Uncle Mats to invite Libbers to groups
- **FR-004**: System MUST restrict story creation capabilities to Uncle Mat role only
- **FR-005**: System MUST restrict story completion (filling blanks) capabilities to Libber role only

#### Story Creation & AI Chat

- **FR-006**: System MUST provide an AI chat interface for Uncle Mats to create stories
- **FR-007**: System MUST generate stories with structured elements including: characters (main characters and antagonist/obstacle), setting, plot structure (beginning/middle/end), moral/lesson, and style
- **FR-008**: System MUST output both complete story text and structured metadata for all story elements
- **FR-009**: System MUST allow Uncle Mats to edit any story element before finalizing
- **FR-010**: System MUST support story types including fairy tales, moral stories, and general short stories
- **FR-011**: System MUST persist saved stories for later editing or madlibization

#### Madlibization Workflow

- **FR-012**: System MUST provide AI-assisted identification of words suitable for becoming blanks, explicitly requesting variety in blank types
- **FR-013**: System MUST identify and label blank types including traditional parts of speech (noun, proper noun, verb, adjective, adverb, interjection, interrogative) and relational word concepts (homophone, synonym, antonym, rhyme) for potential blanks
- **FR-014**: System MUST allow Uncle Mats to approve or reject suggested blanks
- **FR-015**: System MUST allow Uncle Mats to manually add blanks not suggested by the AI
- **FR-016**: System MUST show blanks in the context of the story with blank type labels and reference words (for relational blanks)
- **FR-017**: System MUST allow Uncle Mats to submit completed mad libs to make them available to Libbers

#### Notification System

- **FR-018**: System MUST notify Libbers when new blanks are available for them to fill
- **FR-019**: System MUST notify Libbers when their video is ready to view
- **FR-020**: System MUST notify Libbers when the final story book is complete
- **FR-021**: System MUST support both in-app and push notifications

#### Libber Learning Sessions

- **FR-022**: System MUST present blanks to Libbers in sessions of exactly three words
- **FR-023**: System MUST provide educational content explaining the part of speech for each blank
- **FR-024**: System MUST support educational mini-games related to parts of speech
- **FR-025**: System MUST provide examples showing how the required part of speech can be used
- **FR-026**: System MUST track and save Libber progress and performance on learning activities
- **FR-027**: System MUST allow Uncle Mats to view Libber learning activity data
- **FR-028**: System MUST accept word submissions via voice input
- **FR-029**: System MUST accept word submissions via text input as a fallback
- **FR-030**: System MUST provide positive feedback at the end of each session
- **FR-031**: System MUST inform Libbers they will receive a notification about results

#### Audio Interface & Accessibility

- **FR-032**: System MUST provide audio narration of instructions for Libbers
- **FR-033**: System MUST provide audio narration of content for Libbers
- **FR-034**: System MUST support voice input for Libber answers
- **FR-035**: System MUST be fully functional on mobile and tablet devices with touch-optimized UI

#### Video Generation

- **FR-036**: System MUST generate AI-created cartoon videos for each Libber's word submissions
- **FR-037**: System MUST generate one unique video per Libber per session showing their specific word choices in context
- **FR-038**: System MUST make videos available for viewing once generation is complete
- **FR-039**: System MUST allow Uncle Mats to select one Libber's submission OR create a custom word (combining or editing submissions), which triggers new video generation for the custom word

#### Uncle Mat Review & Feedback

- **FR-040**: System MUST allow Uncle Mats to view all Libber submissions for each blank
- **FR-041**: System MUST allow Uncle Mats to view each Libber's associated video
- **FR-042**: System MUST allow Uncle Mats to select which Libber's word becomes the final version for each blank
- **FR-043**: System MUST allow Uncle Mats to combine words from different Libbers into a single final version
- **FR-044**: System MUST allow Uncle Mats to send personalized feedback messages to individual Libbers
- **FR-045**: System MUST deliver Uncle Mat feedback messages to the appropriate Libber

#### Final Story Assembly

- **FR-046**: System MUST provide an interface for Uncle Mats to arrange video clips in story order
- **FR-047**: System MUST allow Uncle Mats to add AI-generated still images as transitions between clips
- **FR-048**: System MUST support voice recording by Uncle Mat for narration
- **FR-049**: System MUST support text-to-speech generation for narration
- **FR-050**: System MUST synchronize audio narration with the visual timeline of videos and images
- **FR-051**: System MUST produce a final digital story book combining videos, images, and narration
- **FR-052**: System MUST make completed story books available for viewing by all Libbers in the group

#### Content Safety

- **FR-053**: System MUST filter inappropriate content during AI story generation
- **FR-054**: System MUST use AI-based validation to flag potentially inappropriate Libber word submissions
- **FR-055**: System MUST queue flagged content for Uncle Mat review before making it visible to other users
- **FR-056**: System MUST provide moderation tools for Uncle Mats to approve or reject flagged content
- **FR-057**: System MUST prevent flagged content from being displayed to Libbers until Uncle Mat approval

### Key Entities

- **User**: Represents a person using the system with a role (Uncle Mat or Libber), profile information, and group memberships
- **Group**: A collection of users with at least one Uncle Mat and one or more Libbers, associated with shared stories
- **Story**: A narrative with structured elements (characters, setting, plot, moral, style) and complete text, created by an Uncle Mat
- **Story Element**: Individual components of a story including character definitions, setting description, plot points, moral/lesson, and style attributes
- **Mad Lib**: A story with defined blanks, including the base story reference and collection of blanks with their positions and required parts of speech
- **Blank**: A missing word position in a mad lib requiring a specific part of speech, with context and position in story
- **Learning Session**: A set of three blanks presented to a Libber, tracking progress, completion status, and performance
- **Learning Activity**: Educational content or mini-game associated with a part of speech, with completion tracking and performance metrics
- **Word Submission**: A Libber's word for a specific blank, including the word text, timestamp, associated video, and review status
- **Video**: An AI-generated cartoon clip showing a story segment with specific word choices, owned by a Libber
- **Feedback Message**: Communication from Uncle Mat to Libber about their word submission, including encouragement and suggestions
- **Story Book**: The final assembled product combining selected videos, transition images, and narration audio, published to a group
- **Notification**: A message to a user about events (new blanks available, video ready, story complete)

## Success Criteria

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: Uncle Mats can create a complete story from concept to finalized mad lib in under 20 minutes
- **SC-002**: Libbers can complete a three-word learning session in under 10 minutes
- **SC-003**: 90% of Libber voice inputs are successfully transcribed without requiring text fallback
- **SC-004**: Video generation completes within 5 minutes of Libber session completion
- **SC-005**: Libbers show 5-10% improvement in blank type identification accuracy (measured via mini-game performance) after completing 5 learning sessions compared to first session baseline
- **SC-006**: 95% of Libbers successfully complete their first learning session without adult assistance
- **SC-007**: Final story books load and play within 3 seconds on mobile and tablet devices
- **SC-008**: System supports groups with up to 10 Libbers working on the same story simultaneously
- **SC-009**: Uncle Mats provide feedback to at least 80% of Libber submissions
- **SC-010**: Audio narration achieves >80% word recognition in user testing with ages 5-10, using age-appropriate vocabulary (grade 2-4 reading level) and sentence length <15 words
- **SC-011**: System maintains 99% uptime during active hours (6am-midnight), with maintenance windows permitted after midnight
- **SC-012**: AI-based content moderation flags potentially inappropriate submissions within 1 second, queuing them for Uncle Mat review before display to other users

## Assumptions

- Users have reliable internet connectivity for video generation and AI features
- Libbers have adult supervision for initial app setup and account creation
- Target audience is children ages 5-10, with content complexity optimized for ages 8-10
- Libbers primarily use the app during morning (6-9am) and afternoon/evening (2-8pm) hours
- Uncle Mats may use the app throughout the day for story creation and review activities
- Video generation service can handle concurrent requests from multiple users
- AI story generation provides age-appropriate content suitable for children ages 5-10
- Voice input accuracy is sufficient for common English words used by children ages 5-10
- Devices have speakers or headphones for audio narration features
- Standard mobile/tablet devices from the last 3-5 years are sufficient to run the application
- Text-to-speech quality is acceptable for story narration
- AI-generated images and videos are appropriate for children without additional review
- Uncle Mats and Libbers are in the same family or have established trust relationship
- Notifications are acceptable and not overly frequent (avoiding notification fatigue)
- Educational mini-games can be simple and quick (1-2 minutes each)
- Word submission sessions of three words strike the right balance between engagement and cognitive load

## Dependencies

- AI/LLM service for story generation and chat interface
- AI service for identifying suitable mad lib blanks and parts of speech
- Speech-to-text service for voice input transcription
- Text-to-speech service for audio narration
- AI video generation service for creating cartoon clips
- AI image generation service for creating transition images and illustrations
- Push notification service for mobile/tablet notifications
- Content moderation service or API for filtering inappropriate content
- Cloud storage for videos, images, and story books
- Audio recording capability on user devices
